statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n jump lengths - from index i you may move to any index up to i plus its value. Starting at index 0, print yes when the last index is reachable and no otherwise. One pass with one integer: the furthest index reachable so far. At each index, standing beyond the frontier means the walk already failed; otherwise extend the frontier with i plus the jump length, and succeed the moment it covers the last index.

example.why: The frontier runs 2, then 4 - and the last index 4 is already covered.

hint: The reachable indices always form a prefix - its right edge is the whole state.
mistake: Simulating actual jump choices; feasibility needs only the frontier, no path is chosen.
